Design for the end-of-day recap, in both its free and premium forms. Tokens from doc 12; product reasoning from plan doc 11. Interactive: Omelette project `Macros Tracker Native setup`, options **7f** (free) and **7g** (premium).

One screen, three stacked layers. The gate sits between layer 2 and layer 3 and is visible as a design decision rather than a paywall bolted on afterwards.

## Header

`‹ TODAY` and the date, then `YESTERDAY'S RECAP` in accent mono and a one-line verdict at 28px/800:

> A good day with one soft spot.

The verdict is deterministic — chosen from a small set based on which targets were hit — not generated. Free users get it too.

## Layer 1 — Score and totals (free, immediate)

A `82/100` day score, then three rows with a coloured dot each:

| Row | Value | Dot |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Protein floor cleared | `168 / 180` | protein green |
| Calories near target | `1980 / 2150` | protein green |
| Fiber short | `29 / 33` | over-target orange |

Footer: *Scored against the targets that were live on Friday, not today's. Plain arithmetic, no AI, free forever.*

That sentence is load-bearing. The score reads against the day's own `TargetVersion`, so a recap from three weeks ago still means what it meant then.

Note the colour rule holds: `168 / 180` protein is *short* of the floor but still reads green because the day cleared its scoring threshold — orange is reserved for the target that was actually missed.

## Layer 2 — Patterns (free)

Three rows, each a number and a plain-English fact, tagged `FREE`:

* `4/7` — Fiber is your most-missed target this week
* `6/7` — Protein has been on point almost every day
* `−120` — Average calories, week over week

Footer: *These are aggregation queries, not guesses. "You miss fiber 4 days out of 7" is a fact — better computed than prompted.*

Genuinely better computed than prompted. An LLM asked to spot patterns in seven days of numbers will occasionally invent one; a `GROUP BY` will not.

## Layer 3 — Coaching (premium, nightly job)

Tagged `PREMIUM` in accent.

### Locked (7f)

Not a blur. A real description of what the layer does, then three inert placeholder bars, then the CTA:

> **Specific swaps, ready by morning**
> A nightly pass reads the day you actually ate and names the meal that tipped it, with something concrete to try instead. Encouragement first, the nudge second.

`SEE WHAT PREMIUM ADDS`, and below it: *Everything above stays free. The nightly job only runs for accounts that pay for it.*

Blurring real text is a dishonest pattern — it implies content exists that the user is being denied, when in fact the job never ran for them. Describing the feature is both truthful and a better sell.

### Unlocked (7g)

Three cards, in the order doc 11 specifies — **encouragement first, tips second**:

1. `WHAT WENT RIGHT` (green-tinted) — *Six days of hitting protein while in a deficit is the hard part, and you did it again. The salmon dinner alone carried 92g.*
2. `ONE SWAP` — *The caesar wrap at lunch was 690 calories for 6g of fiber. A chicken and black bean bowl lands near 600 with 14g — it would have closed Friday's only gap without touching your protein.*
3. `FOR TOMORROW` — *Fiber is the week's pattern, not one bad day. Berries with the morning oats would put you ahead of it before you leave the house.*

One swap, not a list. The swap must name a specific logged meal with its real numbers — generic advice is what makes AI coaching feel worthless.

Footer row, small and muted: `GENERATED 02:14 LOCAL` · `1 CALL · $0.004`. Arguably for the developer rather than the user, but it belongs in the design: it makes the unit economics visible during the exact period you are deciding what premium costs.

## Where this appears

Deterministic layers are computed on read and available the moment the app opens on the just-completed day. Layer 3 is ready by morning because the job ran overnight. Entry point is the date title or the calendar — no separate tab.

## Implementation notes carried from doc 11

* Nightly job checks the per-user premium flag **before** spending. The flag ships in v1 even though everyone shares the same value
* Job is idempotent per user-day. Re-running produces one result
* "Night" is per-user local time — an hourly sweep finds users whose local day has passed midnight plus a grace buffer, not a single 2am cron
* v1 accepts staleness: analyse once after the buffer, don't regenerate when a past day is edited

## Open

* **Where the recap is surfaced.** A gentle "your recap is ready" is a push notification and its own piece of setup. Undesigned
* **Score formula. **`82/100` is illustrative. The weighting of protein floor vs calorie proximity vs fiber is a product decision, not a design one, and it should be written down before it is coded — an unexplained score erodes trust fast
* **Layer 3 when the day was barely logged.** One entry is not enough material for a swap. It should decline gracefully rather than invent something

## Amendment — 1 Aug 2026 (design review)

1. **The layer-3 lock is now a time gate, not a paywall.** The badge reads `2 OF 4 WEEKS`; the card carries a four-segment progress bar, an unlock date, and the closing line *nothing to buy — keep logging and it turns on by itself*. The `SEE WHAT PREMIUM ADDS` button and the "only runs for accounts that pay for it" line are removed. Reasoning in doc 20; requirement in doc 11.
2. Recap is reached from the menu or from the morning notification, and returns to Today (doc 19).
3. Minimum type size raised to 11px throughout, matching doc 12.
